- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), then gradually converges toward true values.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 77.17 or 79.16), where model predicts even higher values than true outcome.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values are rising sharply (e.g., 81.20, 82.31).
- Mean reversion is implied: model tends to overreact to recent highs and underreact to recent lows, leading to persistent bias.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows a pattern of “early overestimation, late underestimation” — model peaks too early and bottoms too late.
- When history includes a recent spike, model often forecasts a higher peak than actual, then fails to capture the subsequent correction.
- Model does not adjust for the lag between historical price movements and true outcome — it reacts too quickly to recent data, missing longer-term trends.
- Correction should involve dampening early forecast peaks and smoothing out late forecast troughs, especially near the end of the 30-day window.
